items.summary:
GuruFocus

# Nvidia unveils AI breakthrough that goes beyond chatbots

Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials) unveiled its GR00T 2 robotics model and Isaac Lab 3.0 programming tools, advancing its attempts to apply artificial intelligence to physical devices.

The business unveiled the technique at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, Texas. [...] The model may also transfer taught abilities to other robot designs, without the need for being demonstrated on each machine.

Nvidia stated GR0T 2 was among the top three models on a few robotics benchmarks, including RoboCasa365 and RoboLab.

The system may interact with AI agents through an application programming interface, perhaps enabling autonomous systems to coordinate more complicated operations. [...] GR00T 2 is an open robotics world model from the Cosmos platform from Nvidia. It was trained on both robot and human data, including 100,000 hours of open-source video from a person's point of view.

The model was able to do 40 out of 50 jobs it was tested on without task-specific examples, Nvidia says.

GR00T 2 performed successfully on 50 tasks, each with a single demonstration, with a success rate of 71%. That rose to 95% after five demonstrations.

In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge. [...] The researchers then gave the AI that simulation and their Graph-as-Policy framework. The AI generated a robot-control program and repeatedly tested and improved it in simulation. result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ là:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

trong đó $C$ là hằng số tích phân (có thể là bất kỳ số thực nào).

metadata.what_it_tests: Câu hỏi meta → trả lời thẳng, KHÔNG gọi tool.

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu AI (AI Research Assistant) được thiết kế để giúp bạn tìm kiếm, tổng hợp và xử lý thông tin nhanh chóng.

**Những gì tôi làm được:**

🔍 **Tìm kiếm & Thu thập thông tin**
- Tìm kiếm web (tin tức, bài viết, tài liệu) với `lookup`
- Tìm bài báo khoa học trên arXiv với `papers` và đọc full-text với `paper_text`
- Tìm kiếm trên mạng xã hội (X/Twitter) với `social_search` và `timeline`
- Lấy nội dung từ URL bất kỳ với `fetch`
- Tra cứu tài liệu nội bộ với `policy`

📝 **Xử lý & Trình bày dữ liệu**
- Định dạng dữ liệu thành nhiều mẫu: brief, sections, bullets, thread, daily_ai_vn với `format`
- Tóm tắt, tổng hợp, so sánh thông tin từ nhiều nguồn

📤 **Hành động**

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary: “SMASH UP” genuinely unsettled Symphony Hall. Iron-sounding trumpets clashed with the mellow strings. The culmination of the movement was an ear-shattering climax — the brass utterly razing any semblance of prior peace. But the following movements, inseparable from their AI participation, were less captivating. Delays between the musicians’ playing and the system’s processing limited their musical conversation — they lacked any shared sound. The music of the orchestra was divided from the odd, [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”
